text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries, leading to symptoms that develop slowly and worsen over time.
snippet_highlighted_words: develop slowly and worsen over time

list.snippet: Shortness of breath: Usually starts during exercise or climbing stairs and eventually happens at rest.
Fatigue: Feeling very tired or weak during normal daily activities.
Dizziness or fainting: Lightheadedness or fainting spells caused by reduced blood flow and heart strain.
Chest pain or pressure: Discomfort resulting from extra strain on the heart.
Swelling (edema): Fluid buildup causing swollen ankles, legs, feet, or belly.
Heart palpitations: A racing, pounding, or skipping heartbeat.
Cyanosis: Lips, fingers, or skin turning a blue or gray tint due to low oxygen.

text_blocks.snippet: For official guidance and medical details, you can visit the American Lung Association or read the Mayo Clinic Overview.
